sources.entry: Build a Live Code-reloader Library for C++

summary.title: C++ (howistart.org: live code-reloading with premake and dlopen)
summary.one_liner: You learn how C++ builds and links work, how to set up a premake5 project with a shared library, and how to hot-reload a dynamic library at runtime using dlopen/dlsym and a templated RePlexModule wrapper.
keywords: how do c++ programs compile and link
takeaways: C++ source files compile to object files, which are linked into static or dynamic (shared) libraries and executables.
A premake5.lua file declares workspace, configurations, and projects, then generates makefiles or IDE project files per platform.
Dynamic libraries can be loaded, symbol-resolved, and reloaded at runtime with dlopen, dlsym, dlerror, and dlclose on UNIX systems.
Using extern "C" disables name mangling so symbols can be looked up by plain C-string names.
A templated RePlexModule base class wraps loading, symbol caching, and reloading behind a cleaner interface.
summary.summary: This multi-part article walks through the basics of C++ compilation and linking, then sets up a RePlex project with premake5 and a Makefile backend, including a shared library, a runtime executable, and a test library. It builds a minimal hot-reload demo using dlopen, dlsym, and dlclose on UNIX-based systems, then refactors it into a templated RePlexModule class that caches symbol pointers and exposes Execute and GetVar helpers. The page is an in-progress article; the text ends partway through the explanation of variadic templates in Execute.
